title: The role of male hormones in bacterial infections: enhancing Staphylococcus aureus virulence through testosterone-induced Agr activation.
authors: Luo, Zhaoxia; Xi, Huimin; Huang, Wei; Liu, Mei-Fang; Yuan, Lei; Chen, Qiang; Xiao, Yanghua; Zhu, Qing; Zhao, Rui; Sheng, Yi-Yun
one_liner_zh: 研究睾酮通过Agr系统增强金黄色葡萄球菌毒力，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a notorious pathogen predominantly involved in skin and soft tissue infections, exhibiting a distinct innate sex bias. This study explores the influence of testosterone on the virulence of S. aureus and elucidates its underlying mechanisms. Utilizing a skin abscess model in intact and castrated male mice, we assessed the effects of testosterone on S. aureus pathogenicity. Compared to controls, castrated mice showed significantly reduced abscess sizes and decreased bacterial loads, highlighting the role of testosterone in modulating the severity of S. aureus infections. In vitro experiments revealed that testosterone enhances the hemolytic activity, cytotoxicity, and oxidative stress resistance of S. aureus. Real-time quantitative PCR analysis showed a significant upregulation of the genes encoding alpha-hemolysin (hla) and phenol-soluble modulin (psmalpha). Importantly, testosterone treatment significantly enhanced the expression of the accessory gene regulator (Agr) quorum-sensing system components (agrC, agrA, agrB, agrD), while the SaeRS system (saeR, saeS, and sbi) exhibited only slight changes. Gene knockout experiments revealed that deletion of agrC, rather than saeRS and agrBD, abolishes the testosterone-induced enhancement of hemolysis and gene expression, underscoring the key role of AgrC. Molecular docking simulations indicated a direct interaction between testosterone and AgrC protein, with a strong binding affinity at the active site residue SER201. This study provides new insights into the mechanistic basis of how testosterone enhances the pathogenicity of S. aureus, potentially contributing to increased male susceptibility to S. aureus infections and offering a targeted approach for therapeutic interventions.
abstract_zh: 金黄色葡萄球菌（Staphylococcus aureus）是一种臭名昭著的病原体，主要涉及皮肤和软组织感染，并表现出明显的先天性别偏向。本研究探讨了睾酮对金黄色葡萄球菌毒力的影响，并阐明其潜在机制。利用完整和去势雄性小鼠的皮肤脓肿模型，我们评估了睾酮对金黄色葡萄球菌致病性的作用。与对照组相比，去势小鼠的脓肿大小显著减小，细菌载量降低，突显了睾酮在调节金黄色葡萄球菌感染严重程度中的作用。体外实验显示，睾酮增强了金黄色葡萄球菌的溶血活性、细胞毒性和氧化应激抗性。实时定量PCR分析表明，编码α-溶血素（hla）和酚溶性调节蛋白（psmalpha）的基因显著上调。重要的是，睾酮处理显著增强了附属基因调节器（Agr）群体感应系统组分（agrC、agrA、agrB、agrD）的表达，而SaeRS系统（saeR、saeS和sbi）仅表现出轻微变化。基因敲除实验揭示，缺失agrC（而非saeRS和agrBD）消除了睾酮诱导的溶血增强和基因表达变化，强调了AgrC的关键作用。分子对接模拟表明，睾酮与AgrC蛋白之间存在直接相互作用，在活性位点残基SER201处具有强结合亲和力。本研究为睾酮如何增强金黄色葡萄球菌致病性的机制基础提供了新见解，可能有助于解释男性对金黄色葡萄球菌感染易感性增加的原因，并为治疗干预提供了靶向方法。
